svg.title: Mailbox or room
svg.desc: A mailbox and a room compared. Both usually run on the built-in mailbox flow kind; they differ in what the session is and where the talk is kept. A mailbox is declared in a MAILBOX.md in a team folder and opened at boot. The mailbox is one session on the mailbox kind, or on the kind its file names, such as support.desk. Its transcript is mailbox-post items in that one session. Its members are workers named in the file, fixed for that mailbox; when the kind has a notify block, a post wakes them. It can hold a board and route a post to one member. A room belongs to one project, created while the app runs; there is no file and it is never in the inventory. No session is the room: each member of the project has their own talk session on the built-in mailbox kind, and every one reaches the same room. The room's lines are organization data, the room-lines collection, and a member's view reads them; they are not pushed. Its members are the people on the project row, checked on every call. A post wakes the workers in the organization's talk template, which are not members. A room holds no board and routes nothing. Use a mailbox for a standing topic a team owns, set in files, with a board or routing. Use a room for the people on a project talking together, private to them.
svg.text: Usually the same flow kind underneath. What differs is what the session is, and where the talk is kept.
The built-in kind. Every room's talk sessions run on it, and so does a mailbox unless its file names another.

g.text: Declared in MAILBOX.md and opened at boot
The transcript lives in this session
Workers named in the file, fixed for that mailbox.
With a notify block on the kind, a post wakes them.
Hold a board of work to claim and finish.
Route a post to the one member it fits.
Reach for it: a standing topic a team owns.
One per project, made while the app runs. No file
Org data. No session is the room; each holds only which project
People on the project row, checked on every
call. A post wakes the org's template workers.
Hold a board or route a post.
Push lines: each view reads to catch up.
Reach for it: a project's people, talking privately.
Standing topic, set in files, the same workers every time, maybe a board: a mailbox.
A group of people on one piece of work, created at runtime, readable only by them: a project's room.
A one-shot "go do this": neither. Dispatch it into that flow's own session.
